headline: Van Gogh's Starry Night Matches Real July 1889 Sky, Study Reveals
meta_description: New research shows Vincent Van Gogh's iconic painting depicts the actual pre-dawn sky over Saint-Rémy, France on July 22, 1889, matching star clusters and Venu…
summary_short: A joint Korean-space science study reveals Van Gogh's Starry Night matches the real pre-dawn sky from July 22, 1889, painted over 40 years of previous astronomical analy…
body:
For decades, art historians dated Vincent Van Gogh's The Starry Night to June 1889 based on a letter to his brother Theo, but new astronomical research reveals the painting actually depicts the pre-dawn sky over Saint-Rémy, France on July 22, 1889. The study, published in Scientific Reports and conducted jointly by space-science company SLLAB and Kyung Hee University's School of Space Research in South Korea, used advanced shape-analysis methods to match the five central stars in the painting to the Hyades cluster in Taurus—not the Aries constellation suggested by earlier 1980s analyses. The sky that morning featured a waning crescent moon, Venus, and the Hyades cluster all visible together, precisely as Van Gogh rendered them.

The research team's breakthrough came through meticulous detective work. They conducted field trips to France, located the exact spot where Van Gogh stood to sketch the landscape, and reconstructed his view from there. By cross-examining the artist's original French and Dutch letters alongside contemporary weather records and his observations about cicada insects, the researchers proposed that Van Gogh's documented seizure began in late July—not mid-June—leaving July 22 as a plausible painting date. The analysis suggests Van Gogh worked from direct observation rather than imagination, grounding his masterpiece in astronomical reality.

The findings open new doors for understanding Van Gogh's working methods. Researchers now plan to apply the same astronomical techniques to other paintings, including his 1888 work Café Terrace at Night, which may depict the Summer Triangle star formation. "Our conversation with Van Gogh's other skies is still ongoing," said study lead Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim. The intersection of art and astronomy continues to reveal fresh truths about one of history's most beloved paintings.
quick_facts: Study dates The Starry Night to July 22, 1889, not June as previously believed
Research team from South Korea's Kyung Hee University and SLLAB space-science company
Hyades star cluster in Taurus identified as the painting's central stars
First major astronomical re-examination in over four decades
Researchers reconstructed Van Gogh's exact viewing location in Saint-Rémy, France
